topics_and_locators.locator: Chapter 2, §§2.1-2.4, PDF pp.25-33 (printed pp.13-21); standard reversible function query, phase query via |->, phase kickback, query model and Deutsch/DJ/BV computations. Chapter 1 §1.4 and chapter 2 query sections supply circuit/query distinction.

Chapter 2 §2.4, PDF pp.29-33 (printed pp.17-21); Deutsch-Jozsa promise and one-query exact calculation, deterministic classical N/2+1 lower bound and two-random-query bounded-error comparison; Bernstein-Vazirani one-query exact recovery and n-bit classical information lower bound.

Chapter 3 §§3.1-3.3, PDF pp.35-39 (printed pp.23-27); exact Simon promise, post-query coset state, Hadamard/F2 Fourier-sampling law, uniform sample from s-perp, rank-rise probability and expected O(n) samples, Gaussian elimination, and full distributional classical collision lower-bound proof. Exercise 7.13 gives a perfect-success O(n) variant as an exercise, not a proved result in the prose.

Chapter 4, PDF pp.41-48 (printed pp.29-36); cyclic DFT/QFT conventions, exact binary QFT factorization/circuit with output bit reversal, O(n^2) exact count, O(n log n) truncated rotations. Exercise 4.4 asks for the operator-norm/telescoping truncation proof; it is an exercise prompt, not a supplied proof, so QA06 retains a local proof obligation.

Chapter 6 §§6.1-6.2.1, PDF pp.57-60 (printed pp.45-48); characters/finite abelian groups, orthogonality and subgroup annihilators, Fourier/coset facts, and group-structured algorithms. Used as an independent conceptual check, not as a substitute for the audited root suppliers or local finite-dimensional proof.

Chapter 10 §10.1, PDF pp.83–84: HHL explicitly assumes a B-gate state-preparation circuit; chapter 19 §19.3, PDF pp.167–168: efficient preparation of classical vectors is identified as a strong assumption.

topics_and_locators.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.1-1.7, PDF pp.9-12; unitary/query model, computational and oracle costs, reversible embedding by compute-copy-uncompute, promise/query setup. Chapter 21 §§21.1-21.2, PDF pp.105-106, gives a second query-complexity and oracle-access treatment.

No direct Deutsch-Jozsa or Bernstein-Vazirani derivation appears in the complete Childs course chapters assigned for this section. Its query-model and oracle mechanics are corroborating context only; direct QA03 algorithm evidence is de Wolf plus Preskill. This is a documented topic-coverage gap in this source, not a claim of a second direct treatment.

Chapter 6, PDF pp.33-37; finite abelian HSP and Simon specialization, character/Fourier sampling over dual groups and subgroup annihilators. Chapter 4 §4.2, PDF pp.25-28, gives exact binary QFT and Fourier-sampling context.

Chapter 4 §4.2, PDF pp.25-28; binary QFT factorization, gate order and bit reversal, exact O(n^2) gate count, omission of long-distance rotations for O(n log n) gates at inverse-polynomial accuracy. General product error accumulation is discussed in chapter 2, but no detailed QFT truncation-norm proof is supplied; QA06 owns the proof.

Chapter 5 §5.3, PDF pp.29-32, gives an independent deterministic/adversarial classical hidden-subgroup query lower bound; its Simon specialization is corroboration, while QA04 locally proves the stated randomized search bound from an explicit posterior distribution. Chapter 6, PDF pp.33-37, supplies the Simon/finite-abelian HSP algorithm context.

topics_and_locators.locator: §6.1, PDF pp.7-8 (printed pp.1-2); black-box/query cost, reversible function oracle Uf|x>|y> = |x>|y xor f(x)>, and the exact two-Hadamard Deutsch calculation. This chapter does not replace the complete circuit-foundations corpus.

§6.1, PDF pp.8-11 (printed pp.2-5); Deutsch-Jozsa promise and exact one-query interference, deterministic classical N/2+1 cutoff and bounded-error caveat; Bernstein-Vazirani affine inner-product promise, exact one-query recovery, and n classical information bits. This is the independent direct algorithm treatment missing from Childs for QA03.

§6.1, PDF pp.11-13 (printed pp.5-7), plus §6.5, PDF pp.27-33 (printed pp.21-27); exact 2-to-1 Simon promise, coset-pair state, Hadamard sampling from s-perp, independent-equation collection, and Simon as the F_2^n hidden-subgroup case. The course gives O(n) repetitions but not the exact bounded-round tail proposed locally.

§6.2.2, PDF pp.17-18 (printed pp.11-12); positive-sign cyclic QFT, binary phase factorization, exact controlled-rotation circuit, output-bit reversal, n(n-1)/2 controlled rotations, and removal of distant small-angle rotations for O(n log n) gates at stated phase precision. No full operator-norm truncation proof is given.

§6.5.3, PDF pp.30-34 (printed pp.24-28); finite abelian hidden-subgroup characters, annihilator/coset Fourier sampling, and a finite-group sample-count argument. It is cross-check evidence; QA05 uses exact root-local Fourier suppliers and proof contracts.

repository_audit.convention_and_scope: Repository root inner products are linear in the first argument. reading_gaps_and_proof_obligations: Childs’s complete course does not directly derive Deutsch-Jozsa or Bernstein-Vazirani; that source is query-model corroboration only. QA03 direct content is independently covered by both de Wolf and Preskill.

De Wolf presents QFT truncation error as Exercise 4.4, and Childs and Preskill state the O(n log n) approximation without a complete operator-norm proof. QA06 must prove the gate-removal telescoping bound locally; no source exercise is misreported as a proof.

de Wolf’s Simon prose proves exact sample distribution, conditional rank-rise probability and expected O(n) queries, while perfect-success O(n) is left as an exercise. QA04 will prove its own bounded-round failure branch by applying finite-space Markov to the capped finite-prefix query count, with the expected count defined by finite-prefix suprema; its finite-field Gaussian-elimination operation count is also local.

A finite arbitrary-angle controlled-phase gate is not generally an exact word over a fixed finite gate alphabet. QA06 will state exact and truncated counts in the continuous ideal H/controlled-phase alphabet; any Solovay-Kitaev compile count depends on QC12’s exact compiler/error statement and will be tracked separately. A finite-precision classical bit-time for computing arbitrary angle descriptions remains outside the claim unless a precise arithmetic supplier is added.
